subject: Human Body
title: Ulcers and H. Pylori
description: One-minute skill: Ulcers and H. Pylori.

hook.text: For decades, doctors blamed stomach ulcers on stress and spicy food. They were wrong.

buildup.text: In 1982, two Australian scientists found a bacterium called Helicobacter pylori living in stomach acid.

discovery.text: H. pylori burrows under the mucus lining and weakens it. Acid then attacks exposed stomach wall, forming ulcers.

twist.text: Dr. Barry Marshall drank H. Pylori to prove his theory.

climax.text: Most stomach ulcers are now cured with a two-week course of antibiotics, not a lifetime of bland food.

punchline.text: A bacterium, not stress, eats holes in your stomach.
